A quick walkthrough of the main screens and shortcuts.
Show networks as tabs instead of a tree.
Show channel switcher at the bottom of the chat.
Show the nicklist as a resizable side pane instead of a popup. When enabled, the nicklist toggle acts as a persistent show/hide.
Hide messages and DCC offers from specific nicks (per network).
How often to retry when the connection drops.
Automatically rejoin a channel after being kicked. A second kick on the same channel within 60 seconds is not rejoined, to avoid loops against +i/+k/+b modes.
Number of messages to request per channel on join (CHATHISTORY LATEST). Set to 0 to disable.
After the device reboots, reconnect the networks marked auto-connect without opening the app. Requires \"Keep the connection alive\".

Add a network to get started. AfterNET is a good first stop if you are not sure.
TOFU pinning only engages when \"Allow invalid certificates\" is on. The fingerprints below are kept for reference; the current connection is verified by the system CA chain instead.
This server published a Strict Transport Security policy: connections are forced onto TLS and certificate errors cannot be bypassed until the policy expires or the server withdraws it.
Forget STS policy for this host
Tap + to add a server, or edit the ones already here. HexDroid ships with a few defaults.
Tap Connect to open a connection. You can have multiple networks connected at once.
This panel lists every server, channel, and private message you have open. Swipe or tap the ☰ button to show it. Tap any item to switch to it
Type here to chat. Slash commands work too: /join #channel, /msg nick text, /part, /whois nick, /me action text, and more.
This menu reaches channel list, file transfers, ignore list, network settings, and more. It also shows channel mode and topic management when you\'re an op.
Choose a theme, adjust font size, tweak notification sounds, privacy options, and much more. Changes apply instantly.
Enable DCC to send and receive files directly between users. If you\'re behind a router, Passive DCC avoids port-forwarding headaches. SDCC is also supported.
Enter the target nick, then pick a file from storage. Incoming DCC offers also arrive here, accept or reject them from notifications.
Connect to AfterNET and join #HexDroid for support, feature requests, or just to chat with other HexDroid users.
AfterNET isn\'t in your list yet: tap Add AfterNET to add it, then connect and join #HexDroid for support.
You can run the walkthrough again any time from Settings → About. Tap Done to finish.

A short identifier for this device, e.g. \"phone\" or \"hexdroid\". Enables per-client buffers and history when the bouncer supports it (ZNC clientbuffer, soju per-client history). Leave blank to share a single buffer across all clients.

The destination is resolved at the proxy (remote DNS), so .onion addresses work and the server hostname isn\'t leaked to your local network. For Tor, run Orbot and use 127.0.0.1 with port 9050. DCC file sends are routed through the proxy and use passive mode automatically; receiving passive offers and DCC chat hosting are unavailable while a proxy is active, since they require listening outside the tunnel.
Show a notification for server and connection errors. Off by default; transient reconnects never notify.
One sender per line whose messages should never highlight or notify. Use a plain nick, an IRC wildcard (* and ?), or a regular expression wrapped in /slashes/. Messages still appear in their channel.

HexDroid\'s Authenticated Group Messaging. One 256-bit random key, per-message authenticated encryption. You share the key.
